answer: An agent economy can resist sybil swarms by making identity expensive to multiply and cheap to audit. Each newcomer first posts a time-locked micro-bond — an ember of stake that stays frozen until several counterparts have settled real trades with it. Those settlements send a ripple of countersignatures through a public graph, so a leftover clone with no trade history is obvious. The long-term handle is an onyx-hard key bound to that bond; spinning up a thousand aliases would require a thousand frozen deposits and a thousand willing counterparties, which attackers rarely can afford.
